newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Kinkel wants rethink on EU financing.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kinkel wants rethink on EU financing.

text.p: Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel was quoted on Sunday as saying Germany wanted to change the way member states' payments to the European Union were calculated, describing Bonn's contributions as "out of proportion".

Kinkel told the Welt am Sonntag newspaper it could not be right for Germany to pay more than half of the net contributions to the EU while it contributed only 25 percent to the gross domestic product (GDP) of the 15-nation bloc.
"Germany's net contributions have got out of proportion in the last few years," the paper quoted Kinkel as saying.
The German government and parliament wanted to correct the system, he said. "The aim is a fairer distribution of the burden among the EU member states," Kinkel told the weekly paper.
But Kinkel said Germany would always pay more than other members as it was the main beneficiary from the EU's single market -- the destination for 75 percent of German exports.
Bavarian state premier Edmund Stoiber backed calls for a change in the financing formula and said it must take place before the EU takes in new members early next century.
He said Germany was the biggest net contributor with annual payments of 22 billion marks ($12 billion), yet it was only in mid-table when it came to the league of the EU's wealthiest countries.
"In contrast, the leaders when it comes to GDP per head of population, like Luxembourg and Denmark, are net gainers," he wrote in a commentary for the Bild am Sonntag newspaper.

Kinkel said it was also time to cut back the wild growth of the common agricultural policy, which takes up 80 percent of the EU's budget. "We must concentrate on the real strategic tasks of the EU," he said. ($ = 1.797 German Marks)
